From object families to arrow families

The full subcategory spanned by a collection of objects contains exactly the arrows whose endpoints belong to that collection. The formalization uses this observation for coherent families of functors. We explain the endpoint calculation that makes this possible. Use the Chapter 1 structures, the walking morphism, its endpoint data and the Segal axiom. All categories are absolute.

Let \(j\colon J\hookrightarrow C^\simeq \) be a collection of objects, with \(J\) an anima. Let \(M_J\) be the pullback of \(\Map ([1],C)\to C^\simeq \times C^\simeq \) along \(j\times j\). Write \(e_0,e_1\colon \Map ([1],C)\to C^\simeq \) for the endpoint maps and \(m\colon M_J\to \Map ([1],C)\) for its inclusion.

Supplementary Lemma 1. Given \(a\colon T\to \Map ([1],C)\), maps \(x,y\colon T\to J\) and specified comparisons \(e_0a=jx\) and \(e_1a=jy\), there is a lift \(\widetilde a\colon T\to M_J\) with \(m\widetilde a=a\). The collection \(M_J\) is closed under identities and composition.

Proof idea

Pair the endpoint comparisons. Together with \(a\) and \((x,y)\) this gives the full cone defining \(M_J\). Pullback factorization supplies the lift and its first-projection computation. For an identity, use the same chosen object for both endpoints. For a composable pair, the source of its composite is compared with the first source and its target with the second target by the endpoint laws for composition. These supply the required cone for the composite family. □

Supplementary Lemma 2. Let \(i\colon A\to C\) be a subcategory presentation of \(M_J\). Suppose \(\Gamma \) is an anima and we have functors \[ h\colon \Gamma \to \Map (D,C),\qquad k\colon \Gamma \to \Map (D^\simeq ,J), \] together with an identification \(j_*k=r_Dh\), where \(r_D\) is the action on objects. Then there is a family \(\widetilde h\colon \Gamma \to \Map (D,A)\) with \(i_*\widetilde h=h\).

Proof idea

Let \(a(h)\) be the action of \(h\) on arrows, with values in \(\Map (\Map ([1],D),\Map ([1],C))\). For either endpoint \(e\), naturality of the mapping action under restriction gives \[ (e^*)_*a(h)=j_*(e^*)^*k. \] The \(e^*\) on the left is endpoint evaluation in \(C\); the one on the right is endpoint evaluation in \(D\). This equation retains the given comparison on objects.

Uncurry \(a(h)\) to obtain a family of arrows indexed by \(\Gamma \times \Map ([1],D)\). The two endpoint equations allow Supplementary Lemma 1 to lift this family through \(M_J\). Curry back, using that \(\Gamma \) is an anima. Now \(h\) and its lifted arrow action form a cone for the subcategory presentation tested at \(D\). Factor that cone; its first computation is \(i_*\widetilde h=h\). □

Supplementary Corollary 3. Let \(i\colon A\to C\) be a full subcategory and \(f\colon D\to C\) a functor. A specified factorization of \(f^\simeq \) through \(i^\simeq \) gives a factorization \(\widetilde f\colon D\to A\) with \(i\widetilde f=f\). Any two such factorizing functors are identified.

Proof idea

Name \(f\) and its coherent object factorization. They give a cone for the mapping-anima pullback characterizing the full subcategory. Factor this cone and decode its first-projection comparison. For two factorizations, combine their comparisons with \(f\) and reflect through the embedding \(i\). The uniqueness declaration linked here compares the underlying functors; a prescribed comparison between the complete factorization triangles is not separately asserted by it. □
